{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Richard Earl Block''' (born 1931) is an American [[mathematician]]. He was a [[distinguished professor]] at the [[University of California, Riverside]] who works on [[Lie algebras]] over [[field (mathematics)|field]]s of prime [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]].

Block earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1956 under the supervision of [[Abraham Adrian Albert]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6459}}</ref> He was the first to discover the [[central extension (mathematics)|central extension]] of the [[Witt algebra]] that gives the [[Virasoro algebra]], though his discovery went unnoticed for many years. With Robert Lee Wilson he classified the simple Lie algebras over "well behaved" fields of finite characteristic. 

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Richard E. Block,  [https://www.jstor.org/stable/1994485 ''On the Mills–Seligman axioms for Lie algebras of classical type''],  [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]], 121  (1966),  pp.&nbsp;378–392. (The paper that gives the central extension defining the Virasoro algebra.)
*Richard E. Block and Robert Lee Wilson,  [http://www.pnas.org/cgi/content/abstract/81/16/5271 The Restricted Simple Lie Algebras are of Classical or Cartan Type], [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]  August 15, 1984  vol. 81, no. 16, 5271–5274.
